notes.title: Update 1.3.5
notes.notes:
Long time no see!

I had been doing some silent hotfixes here and there since last official update 1.3.4. They were really too minor to be worth posting about.

But not this time!

There has been an annoying bug for a while that I just couldn't track down. Some users finally messaged me about it and I decided it was time to really put some thought into it. And so I did for a second...

One thing I could do was to try and hunt it down. Which would likely be tedious as it was a really weird one.

The other thing I could do was simply erase the whole module where the bug was obviously residing and do it over from scratch.

I opted for the latter.

Doing so didn't take as nearly as much time as you'd think. I had a good idea of what I was doing. The new version was tested for a few days and the bug seems to have disappeared. And today it's finally yours. Enjoy!

Bug fixes :

 Pressing Ctrl without its other keybinded keys would sometime trigger Quixer and you'd get a volume pop-up as if you were lower the volume of an app.
 Fixed another startup bug.
 Other minor improvements.

notes.title: Update 1.3.4
notes.notes:
Always more bugs

There was yet another bug stopping users with a certain configuration from using Quixer. I apologize again to you if that was your case!

That has now been fixed!

I bring a gift as an apology!

The Playback Devices feature was changed to Audio Devices because it now includes Recording devices!

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33706882/a4440219c744574d9102dbe7671624dd2cf28756.png

As you can see, there are now two colors of devices. Purple representing playback devices, and blue representing recording devices.

It works exactly the same way. There will now be a tray icon for each type of device. If you're not using the feature for either playback or recording devices, you can disable their tray icon respectively in the Settings.

Have fun!

notes.title: Update 1.3.3
notes.notes:
IT'S FIXED! SORRY!

I apologize to the few who bought the application between yesterday and today. I had introduced a major bug in update 1.3.2 without realizing.

That has now been fixed and everything should start up normally.

ːsteamfacepalmː

Edit :
If you are still getting an error when you launch, it might be that your config file is corrupted beyond repair. 

You will have to go here : 
C:\Users\[Username]\AppData\Roaming\Senerio\Quixer and delete config.json. 

It should be fine after that. If not, make sure you get in touch with me.

notes.title: Update 1.3.2
notes.notes:
We have yet another quality of life improvement!

You can now decide what goes into the Toggle Device feature sequence.

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33706882/f0662412b8347df83c4b2b80f5f821c920bc10f0.png

By default, any device you add will be inserted in the sequence. If you wish to take it out, simply uncheck the option circled in the image above.

To make it clear, here's a small example situation in which you would need this option :

We have 3 devices (A, B and C) we switch between. So we set all 3 devices in Quixer. Now only A and B are used on a daily basis. C is more situational and is not used enough to justify having to go over it every time we use the toggle device function.

And so, by deactivating the option shown above for device C, when we're toggling between devices, only A and B are going to be in the rotation. C will remain available by other means, such as the tray icon context menu or a specific hotkey.

And that's it! Sweet and simple like that.

Bug fixes

I had introduced a bug with the last update. Hotkeys were overlapping, causing multiple action to be executed at the same time. Namely (if you kept it on default) Volume Up, Faster Volume Up and Volume Reset. 

That has now been fixed along with one or two other minor bugs.

notes.title: Update 1.3.1
notes.notes:
Just a quick hello to say it is now possible to distinguish between the same modifier keys.

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33706882/38bb3431847883b7f308c05f50822dbe1e5fafc4.png

The little white corner indicates there's a tip for that key. In this case, it will tell you that you can rotate between Ctrl, LCtrl and RCtrl by clicking on the key.

This means that if you set your hotkey to LCtrl + A and press RCtrl + A, Quixer won't detect it as the correct hotkey. If you set it to Ctrl + A, there is no change from before, both LCtrl and RCtrl will work.

Cheers!

notes.title: Update 1.3.0
notes.notes:
It's update time again!

I've been working on a requested feature these past few days and I'm glad to announce it's now released!

Here comes the Volume Preset feature!

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33706882/211aa7884b14764b1f480dbb6086d15c245fd225.png

I've had a few requests and I've done a bit of research on the topic. While it might not be as useful as the two other features for the majority of people, there was definetely a demand for it and I thought it would be a good asset to have in order to gain a wider appeal.

What this feature essentially allows you to do is make different presets under different hotkeys. Each preset can be loaded with different applications and each application can have its own volume level.

When a hotkey for a preset is used, Quixer will set the volume of each applications to the values you configured. If you have different volume setups when doing different activities, this will definetely come in handy.

New UI pop-up simple view:
https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33706882/078295cd2e5b770c64841ace4c9236364fef0061.png

New UI pop-up detailed view:
https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33706882/c1bc6fb796ba74144a9059f9af7bf28f68e806e5.png

But that's not all!

If you don't know that yet, every time I touch my code, I also look at older features for things to improve! And sure enough, this time around is not an exception to that rule!

Here's a list

Fixed the crash occuring when checking the Show Numerical Value and Show 'Other Applications' Caption 
Added the possibility to enable/disable each of the UI pop-ups
Added a Fade Out Timer for each UI pop-ups
Changed a few things in the configs (sorry 3 or 4 settings might be back to default values)
Furthered the re-designed of the Settings tab
A few other minor UI changes
The usual tiny bug squasing


What now?

The quest for improvement continues. While that's undergoing, I've decided to increase Quixer's price tag to $3 USD (from $2 USD) as it has become a bigger package. I've also re-written the store page's description to be more descriptive and appealing. 

The last thing I want to do before starting to work on a new feature again is record and edit a new trailer. The current one has a special place in my heart, but it's missing a lot of what became key elements after a few months of receiving updates.

And that's about it folks! My report is complete! I'll now be enjoying some games after this bit of hard work!

notes.title: Update 1.2.7
notes.notes:
It was cold today here in Canada so I decided to stay inside and work on Quixer....... As if I need an excuse to stay inside...

AHEM! That said...

I got some goodies for you tonight!

Here comes the brand new device change pop-up!

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33706882/0b387174dc4ed50a07e8362955c772d02265e22f.png

Fear not! If you actually don't want to see it, I have added a new setting that allows you to hide not only the new device pop-up, but the volume slider as well! 

Still, I would appreciate if you didn't hide it because I worked meticulously on it hehe.

In order to add that feature I reworked a notable part of my code once again. I tested the features a bunch and there didn't seem to be any issue. Keep an eye out and notify me ASAP if you spot anything!

That was the main selling point for today but I also have a few other improvements I'd like to mention :

- Worked back and forth on my code and design and hopefully made the UI more responsive and fluid overall.
- Quixer won't prevent Windows from shutting down anymore!
- I rearranged the Settings tab in what I think is a better layout for understanding what kind of various options there are.
- Squashed a few hidden bugs.

And that's it! Thanks to the following user for suggesting their ideas! 
It sure was possible "at some point". ;)

I love the new audio device switch feature! There are, however, two improvements I hope are possible at some point.

1. A UI pop-up like the volume controls that shows what you are switching to.
2. Having this feature on prevents Windows from shutting down. I have to force close Quixer before I can do so.

Keep the feedback coming everyone!

notes.title: Update 1.2.0
notes.notes:
Merry Christmas! 

I hope you're all having a good time with the people close to you!

With university done for a while, I had spare time on my hands and I didn't know what to make of it! And so I decided to finish the feature I had started back before finals started.

I present to you the Quixer Playback Devices Quick Change Feature! (I didn't find a better name. Sorry!)

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33706882/dae7480217e8a1fd36c3aeaa0fa9649588b28923.png

Well, the name kind of says it all really. For those of you who have speakers, headphones or a headset that they often change between depending on the time of day or activity they're undertaking, myself first, this is a feature designed with you just in mind!

This will allow you to setup your various devices in Quixer and change between them at the push or click of a few buttons without having to go deep inside Windows just to change the sound input device. In reality Quixer will do those steps for you but instead of taking 10 seconds of your precious time it's going to take 0.6333333 second (exact science).

I plan on making a new trailer video to show this feature. So if you don't understand what it does and/or if it's good for you, wait a little bit!

For now that was a present from me to you on these festive times! As always, if you encounter a bug or want to give some feedback, my Discord Server or the Steam Discussions are awaiting you!

Happy Holidays folks!

notes.title: Update 1.1.4
notes.notes:
Sorry there was no patchnotes the last couple updates. They were only tiny hotfixes. Here's a little list of what has happened since 1.1.0.

- Added two new settings to help you keep your profiles in sync
- Performance improvements
- Bug fixes (namely muting was behaving oddly)

Also added a Discord Link in the About tab. If you have anything you'd like to ask you can come in any time. I sometime sleep but I'm very active otherwise!

That's it for today!

notes.title: Update 1.1.0
notes.notes:
I was hard at work this past week between exams and Quixer. I got some juicy stuff for you!

A few were asking for more and more keys to bind hotkeys on. With different keyboard layouts and exotics keys, I had to go with what made the most sense.

And so! I got rid of the keyboard layout and redesigned the keybinding from scratch. You can now simply press the keys you want to assign as a hotkey and some mysterious magic will happen right before your eyes.

Next we have profiles! This feature had me re-design the way configurations were handled so you will unfortunately have to rebind your hotkeys. (Sorry!)

I will try to make this simple... You have the default profile which is Global Profile. This profile is the equivalent of how Quixer used to be. Meaning the focused window will be the one having its volume adjusted.

You can add more profiles that will target exes of your choice. Upon assigning hotkeys to those profiles, you will be able to manage their audio without the need to be focused on those apps.

I'm sure it will make more sense when you try it!

And finally, as you can probably see, Quixer got a nice design overhaul all around. Don't underestimate designing... it takes a lot of time.

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33706882/340ea235cb1676215508d082c994160db6af3d9a.png

Even though I tested the new features a bunch, there might still be a few bugs hiding around. If you encounter one make sure you report it. 

Feedback is always welcomed so keep it coming.

That's it for now though. Profiles have opened a door to more features in the future so we will see what happens next!
